rationale: The Catechism names 'the sign of the temple' alongside the sign of Jonah as Christ's announcement of his death and rising on the third day. Medium: terse, and the temple figure (John 2:19-21) is identified only by name.

type.name: Jesus Raising the Dead
type.description: The dead whom Jesus restored to earthly life during his ministry: the daughter of Jairus, the widow's son at Nain, and Lazarus (Mark 5:41-42; Luke 7:14-15; John 11:43-44).

alternatives_considered.why_not: the antitype itself; these raisings were returns to earthly life, 'of another order' (§994, §646)
a person; the paragraph names his acts of raising the dead

type.reasoning: The type is Jesus' raisings of the dead during his ministry. No catalog Type names them.

alternatives_considered.why_not: the paragraph speaks of bodily resurrection, not eternal life in general

antitype.reasoning: The resurrection of believers on the last day, of which the raisings are 'a sign and pledge', and Christ's own Resurrection, which they announce.

quote: Already now in this present life he gives a sign and pledge of this by restoring some of the dead to life, announcing thereby his own Resurrection, though it was to be of another order.
rationale: The raisings are 'a sign and pledge' of the last-day resurrection and 'announce' Christ's own. Both sides are in the New Testament, so nt-figure; medium because 'sign and pledge' is sign language rather than figure language.
